name: 911 Batch Repeater
description: Finds repeat parts for a 911 QTDR batch via the 911 MASTER PARTS LIST (compiled from completed nests). The two-phase Sentry Drone picker locks the batch folder, zooms inside, then multi-locks the nests to run before striking them - or, with the drone off, a folder dialog plus a nest-selection window with per-nest grab toggles (SolidWorks models, part PDFs, overwrite). Copies each repeat part's CAD folder from its completed source nest into a REPEAT folder inside the target nest.
author: Anthony Sieben

setup: Sync the '911 QTDR' folder. The batch you're repeating into must already be set up (its nest folders exist).
Make sure the 911 Master Parts List in the REPEATER folder is up to date - the app looks up repeat parts in it.
The completed source nests need their CAD-AND-SHOP-PRINTS folders on disk (models + PDFs) so there's something to copy.
how_it_works: Target the batch, then lock the nests you want repeats for (Sentry Drone mode gives the two-phase picker; turn it off in Settings for a plain dialog).
For each selected nest it looks up every part's number in the Master Parts List and finds the completed nest that already made it.
It copies each repeat part's SolidWorks models and PDF from that source nest into the target nest's REPEAT folder.
output: A REPEAT folder inside each selected nest, with one subfolder per repeat part holding its models and PDF.
A run summary of what was pulled, what had no usable source, and what was only ever made in this nest.

fields.label: 911 QTDR Root
fields.description: The 911 QTDR folder (live batch folders + the REPEATER folder under 04 - Notes - Protocols - Tutorials \ TECH SERVICES). Leave blank to auto-detect under your OneDrive Pilot Program folder.

fields.label: Master Parts List
fields.description: The 911 MASTER PARTS LIST.xlsx to look repeat parts up in. Leave blank to use the copy in the REPEATER folder.

fields.label: Sentry Drone mode
fields.description: Pick the batch folder through the targeting-drone kill-cam - crosshair cursor, lock-on, and a railgun strike on the folder. Turn off for a normal folder dialog.
